product: ARD-101, an oral gut-restricted bitter-taste-receptor (TAS2R) agonist that triggers local CCK, GLP-1 and PYY satiety signalling, being developed for hyperphagia in Prader-Willi Syndrome (FDA Orphan Drug and Rare Pediatric Disease designations). ARD-201, a fixed-dose ARD-101 plus DPP-4 inhibitor combination, was aimed at obesity. No product generates revenue; both programs are paused (2026-05-07).
demand: Not applicable: Aardvark is a pre-revenue clinical-stage company with no product sales to decompose into price, volume or mix. FY2025 revenue was zero and H1 2026 net loss was $36.0M; all value comes from binary trial and regulatory progress, not pricing or unit growth (2026-08-11).
pricing_power: No product margins exist to collapse. The real risk is cash burn and dilution: H1 2026 net cash used in operations was $36.5M, accumulated deficit reached $151.9M at 2026-06-30, runway is into late 2027, and a $150M at-the-market facility under a $400M shelf registration can dilute holders if the program continues (10-Q 2026-08-11).
competition: No Chinese or other low-cost generic substitute was identified for Prader-Willi hyperphagia. The approved alternative is Soleno's VYKAT XR (diazoxide choline ER, FDA-approved March 2025). Generic diazoxide is not approved for PWS hyperphagia. Not found otherwise.
market_strategy: 2026-02-27 CEO Tien Lee: we are committed to advancing the ARD-101 clinical program and we are evaluating optimal therapeutic dosing levels. 2026-05-14 Tien Lee: we remain committed to advancing ARD-101 as a potential therapy for this underserved patient population. 2026-08-11 Tien Lee: in the third quarter of this year, we are assessing the unblinded data from the HERO and OLE trials.
bull: Cash of $73.9M (about $3.34/share) funds operations into late 2027, and the promised Q3 2026 unblinded HERO and OLE data could still be released by 2026-09-30, potentially informing a path forward with the FDA.
bear: Phase 3 HERO and OLE were terminated in June 2026, the FDA full clinical hold since 2026-05-14 blocks ARD-101, no product revenue exists, and securities class actions plus a $150M ATM create dilution and legal overhang.
falsifier: By 2026-09-30, Aardvark releases unblinded HERO and OLE data showing meaningful hyperphagia reduction with no cardiac QRS signal, and the FDA lifts the 2026-05-14 full clinical hold.
web_what_changed_30_90d: Last 30d (since 2026-08-28): no company press release; only securities-litigation notices - Robbins LLP probe 2026-09-17, Lowey Dannenberg probe 2026-09-18, SueWallSt reminder 2026-09-25 with lead-plaintiff deadline 2026-10-13; RBC (2026-09-24) said the ARD-101 path forward may be challenging. web_true_now_not_modelled: The promised Q3 2026 unblinded HERO and OLE readout is still unreported as of 2026-09-27 although Q3 ends 2026-09-30 (2026-08-11 PR). The Phase 3 HERO and OLE trials were TERMINATED, not merely paused, in June 2026, so no near-term approval path exists without new trials. Cash $73.9M equals $3.34/share net cash versus a $5.06 close on 2026-09-25; a $150M ATM sits unused under a $400M shelf; a separate dermatology subsidiary led by CEO Bryan Jones exists since 2026-02-12.
web_demand_product: ARD-101, an oral gut-restricted bitter-taste-receptor (TAS2R) agonist that triggers local CCK, GLP-1 and PYY satiety signalling, being developed for hyperphagia in Prader-Willi Syndrome (FDA Orphan Drug and Rare Pediatric Disease designations). ARD-201, a fixed-dose ARD-101 plus DPP-4 inhibitor combination, was aimed at obesity. No product generates revenue; both programs are paused (2026-05-07).

FY2025 revenue was zero and H1 2026 net loss was $36.0M; all value comes from binary trial and regulatory progress, not pricing or unit growth (2026-08-11).
web_bottleneck: The FDA full clinical hold on the ARD-101 IND since 2026-05-14, tied to reversible cardiac observations (QRS prolongation) at above-target doses in a healthy-volunteer study disclosed 2026-02-27, is the binding constraint. A secondary bottleneck was Phase 3 HERO enrolment difficulty, which forced a 2026-02-10 protocol amendment lowering eligibility to children aged 7 and older.
web_who_benefits_next: Soleno Therapeutics benefits most while the hold lasts: its VYKAT XR (diazoxide choline extended-release) was the first FDA-approved Prader-Willi hyperphagia therapy in March 2025 and faces less competition with ARD-101 halted. Second-order beneficiaries: short sellers and the plaintiff bar (Robbins, Pomerantz, Hagens Berman, Lowey Dannenberg) now litigating AARD.
web_who_loses: If AARD revives and wins, Soleno Therapeutics loses most, since its approved VYKAT XR would face a differentiated oral hunger-targeting therapy. In the current direction AARD holders have already lost: shares fell 56% (about $7.02) after the 2026-02-27 pause and a further 32.1% after the 2026-05-14 FDA full clinical hold, per Hagens Berman and Pomerantz.
web_margin_collapse_risk: No product margins exist to collapse. web_low_cost_substitute: No Chinese or other low-cost generic substitute was identified for Prader-Willi hyperphagia. The approved alternative is Soleno's VYKAT XR (diazoxide choline ER, FDA-approved March 2025). Generic diazoxide is not approved for PWS hyperphagia. Not found otherwise.

web_did_they_deliver: Delivered: the guidance promised for Q2 2026 on 2026-02-27 was given on 2026-05-07 (Q1 results) and 2026-05-14 (FDA hold and unblinding plan). Missed: the original HERO topline Q3 2026 guidance, which the company itself withdrew on 2026-02-27, and the 2026-02-10 age-7+ protocol expansion, made moot when HERO was terminated in June 2026. Open: the 2026-05-14 unblinding promise, reaffirmed 2026-08-11.
web_what_would_falsify: Aardvark releasing, by the end of Q3 2026-09-30, unblinded HERO and OLE data showing ARD-101 meaningfully reduces hyperphagia with no cardiac QRS safety signal, followed by the FDA lifting the full clinical hold placed 2026-05-14, would break the bear case. Conversely, no data release by 2026-09-30 plus a continuing hold confirms it.
